title: Mets trading reliever A.J. Minter to the Twins as deadline sell-off begins for New York
author: Tim Britton
content:
The New York Mets’ trade-deadline selloff started late Thursday night when they traded lefty reliever A.J. Minter to the Minnesota Twins for two prospects, people close to the situation confirmed. Those people spoke on condition of anonymity to freely discuss a deal that had not yet been announced.

New York is landing prospects Bruin Agbayani and Billy Amick in the deal, which came ahead of the MLB’s trade deadline, set for Monday at 6 p.m. ET.

A 19-year-old shortstop who bats left-handed, Agbayani brings a name that will be familiar to Mets fans of a certain age. His father, Benny, played four of his five big-league seasons with the Mets, from 1998 to 2001. The elder Agbayani was a key part of the 2000 team that lost to the New York Yankees in the famed Subway Series.

Bruin Agbayani was drafted in the sixth round in 2025, with the 179th pick.

Minter, 32, has been one of the game’s best late-game left-handed relievers for nearly a decade, wielding a hard fastball and one of baseball’s best cutters. Most of that work was done with the Atlanta Braves, posting a 3.28 ERA over eight seasons while serving as a primary set-up man and occasional closer. He excelled in the postseason, especially during the club’s run to the 2021 championship. Overall, he’s posted a 2.88 ERA in the playoffs.

While Minter’s effectiveness hasn’t waned, a pair of serious injuries and some questionable peripherals follow him. He missed the end of the 2024 season because of surgery to repair a torn labrum in his hip, then was out for 13 months because of surgery on his left lat in May 2025. Since returning from the lat procedure, his fastball velocity has dipped 2 mph and his strikeout rate has fallen back to league average. His walk rate has also plummeted, but he’s unlikely to keep it quite as low as it is right now.

Minter is owed $3.3 million after Monday before becoming a free agent this offseason. The Mets are not paying down any of the remaining salary, said a person with knowledge of the situation.

ESPN first reported the news.

Amick, the other prospect involved in the deal, was the Twins’ second-round pick in 2024, out of the University of Tennessee. The 23-year-old third baseman has 23 home runs in 86 games at Double-A Wichita this year, with a .217 average and .338 on-base percentage.

The trade deadline is supposed to contribute to a course correction for the last-place Mets and their fans, who both had such high hopes to begin the year. At 47-63, the Mets’ .427 winning percentage is better than only two other teams in the National League — a great disappointment for a club that entered Thursday carrying the second-highest payroll in the majors, at about $374 million, per Cot’s Contracts.

The Mets let stars such as Pete Alonso and Edwin Díaz leave via free agency last offseason, and president of baseball operations David Stearns’ plan to retool has missed the mark — at least in the short term. Now, at this year’s deadline, he has a chance to further shape the team as he wants. But the next few days will be trying for Mets fans, as Stearns will likely send more talent away via trade.

This story will be updated.
